n: In August 1842 Missouri officials sought to extradite Joseph on false charges connected with an attempt on former governor Lilburn Boggs’s life. Joseph went into hiding and wrote this letter on September 1, explaining he had left his affairs in good hands and would return when the storm passed.

f.w: my enemies, both in Missouri and this State
f.g: Missouri sought Joseph’s arrest as an accessory in the 1842 shooting of Lilburn W. Boggs; Joseph was later freed by a federal judge in January 1843.

n: Joseph reflects that envy and anger have followed him all his life—perhaps because he was foreordained for a purpose. “Deep water” is familiar to him; like Paul, he glories in trials because God has always delivered him.

f.w: deep water is what I am wont to swim in
f.g: Wont = accustomed. Trouble had become normal for him.

f.w: ordained from before the foundation of the world

n: The Saints should rejoice: Israel’s God is their God and will justly repay their oppressors.
The Lord commands that temple building continue without stopping, with redoubled diligence. Persecution is nothing new; the prophets endured it, and heaven holds a reward.
Joseph now gives instructions about baptism for the dead.
Each baptism for the dead must have a recorder who personally sees and hears it, so he can testify truthfully. Witnesses and records make the ordinance valid.
What is properly recorded on earth will be recorded in heaven—the binding and loosing power Jesus gave Peter.

f.w: whatsoever you bind on earth, may be bound in heaven

n: The Lord is about to restore much more pertaining to the priesthood—fulfilled in the Nauvoo temple ordinances.
Records must be kept orderly and stored in the temple archives for future generations—a foundation of the Church’s family history work.

f.g: A place where important records are preserved.

n: Joseph had wanted to preach about baptism for the dead the next Sunday, but in hiding he will write the Lord’s word and send it by mail.

f.g: From the speaker’s platform at a public meeting.

n: He must close quickly; enemies are watching. Quoting Jesus, he says Satan “hath nothing in me”—no hold over him.

f.w: the prince of this world cometh, but he hath nothing in me

n: Joseph prays that all may be saved and signs as their servant and prophet.
